scripts.title: The Pillar
scripts.sport: rugby
scripts.place: One background: an old rugby stand on a bright cold afternoon, seen from the pitch side (her phone is between them and the pitch, so we look back up the stand). Soft rows of fans in scarves rising behind them, a low roof with dark girders, a strip of pale sky top left. No signs, no numbers, no crest. On its own layer: one fat cream-painted steel roof pillar with rivets, close to the lens, about a third of the frame wide, soft at the edges.
scripts.hook: Luna's face close and sunny, hair blowing. A fat roof pillar fills the right third of the picture, and from behind it peeks half of Timo's face: one heavy-lidded eye, looking at us.

lines.text: They were the last two together!
Why do you think that was?

lines.direction: generous, quick, sure it solves everything
after a short pause, dry, kind

scripts.picture: The lens is the pitch: when they look at us they are watching the match. SHOT 1 (0.0-5.4), her usual framing; the pillar layer stands on our right in front of Timo and at rest hides the right half of his face. 0.0 Luna sunny, to us: 'Rugby! Great seats!' Timo: one eye, on us. 1.4 he leans toward her, out past the pillar (both eyes and his mouth come clear): 'I have a pillar.' He settles back behind it. 3.0 Luna guilty (sideways look at him): 'They were the last two together!' JUMP CUT closer (5.4-11.75). 5.4 Timo leans out, eyes on her: 'Why do you think that was?' 7.7 a 0.45 s beat: Luna guilty, crooked smile; he goes back behind the pillar. 8.15 ROAR, the picture jolts; Luna's eyes snap to us, sunny, shouting: 'Did you see that?!' 10.1 Timo, one eye, not moving (teal caption, her mouth shut): 'No.' 10.85 Luna turned to him: 'Fine. Swap.' WHIP (11.75). SHOT 2 (12.05-19.55), wider by 15 per cent, a new take: the same pillar is now on our LEFT across half of Luna's face (one big eye, half a smile); Timo stands clear on the right, upright, eyes on us. 12.05 Luna, sunny with one eye: 'It's not that bad!' 13.7 ROAR, bigger, jolt. Luna: caught (one worried eye). 14.4 Timo, eyes on us, mild: 'Oh, that was lovely.' 16.1 Luna, caught: 'What happened?' Music stops dead. 17.25 Timo, eyes on her: 'You'd have loved it.' 18.8 hold 0.75: his eyes come to us, the flat look; her one eye on us, a small pout. ENDS on that. 19.55 plate 2.4 s (total 21.95).
new_drawings: Background: old rugby stand seen from the pitch side, soft crowd, low roof
The roof pillar on its own layer (stands on the right over Timo, then on the left over Luna; the same drawing)
scripts.who_wins: Timo. He takes her seat, sees the best moment of the match and keeps it to himself. He is in the clear and on his feet at the end.
scripts.sounds: Open-air rugby crowd, a referee's whistle far off. Two roars (8.15 and, bigger, 13.7). Her vlog music from 0.0; it stops dead at 17.0, just before 'You'd have loved it.'; the stare plays over crowd murmur only.
scripts.why_funny: She solves his restricted view by swapping, and the next roar belongs to him; every travelling fan has paid for a seat and watched a pillar.

scripts.title: Safety Car
scripts.sport: motor racing
scripts.place: One background: the catch fence at a race track from the front rows of a grandstand: wire fence close behind them, the track a grey band, a far grandstand roof, bright overcast sky. Cars exist only as streaks of colour moved in the edit. No boards, no logos, no numbers.
scripts.hook: Luna close, mouth wide in a cheer, a small plain flag flapping in her raised hand. Behind her Timo in huge orange ear defenders, eyes shut, perfectly still, as a streak of colour tears past the fence.

lines.text: Motor racing! I've picked a driver!
Lights on the roof. He's winning!

lines.direction: slow, as to a friend he likes
after a long look, flat, a cheer with no cheer in it

scripts.picture: SHOT 1 (0.0-5.6), widest, fence and track behind. 0.0 an engine screams past (a streak right to left), her hair and scarf whip; Luna sunny, shouting, her free hand up from below with a small flag: 'Motor racing! I've picked a driver!' Timo in ear defenders, eyes shut. 2.4 his eyes open, on her: 'Which one?' 3.25 Luna to us, the flag waving on 'winning': 'Lights on the roof. He's winning!' JUMP CUT closer (5.6-12.3). 5.65 Timo leans to her: 'That's the safety car.' 7.25 Luna sunny: 'He's in front.' 8.45 Timo, eyes on her: 'He's not in the race.' 10.4 Luna turned to him: 'Then why's nobody passing him?' JUMP CUT tighter, both faces (12.3-18.6). 12.35 Timo: 'They're not allowed.' 13.55 Luna, still turned to him, amazed: 'So he can't lose!' 15.1 music stops dead. Timo's eyes go to us: 0.75 s. Luna turns back to the lens, sunny, the flag up. 15.85 his eyes narrow for 0.45 s (he is working it out and finds no hole in it). 16.3 eyes on us again, flat: '...Come on, safety car.' One low engine burbles past; Luna waves the flag. Hold 0.7. ENDS: Luna waving and beaming, Timo in ear defenders with the flat look into the lens. 18.6 plate 2.4 s (total 21.0).
new_drawings: Background: race-track catch fence from a grandstand, overcast
Timo, same pose, wearing big orange ear defenders (face free)
Luna's free hand holding a small plain green-and-cream flag, no emblem
scripts.who_wins: Luna's logic stands. Timo is right about every fact, cannot fault her conclusion and changes sides with his dignity whole. On his feet at the end.
scripts.sounds: Race-track bed: engines far round the circuit, tannoy mumble with no words. One loud pass at 0.0, one slow low pass at 17.0. Her vlog music from 0.0; it stops dead at 15.1 on 'So he can't lose!'.
scripts.why_funny: The friend who cheers for the wrong thing turns out to have picked the only car that cannot lose, and the expert joins her; anyone who has stood at a track knows the safety car leads more laps than their driver.

scripts.title: Really Slowly
scripts.sport: tennis
scripts.place: One background: the top rows of an outdoor tennis stand on a still sunny afternoon, looking down over their shoulders: soft rows of sunhats seen from behind, then the green court small and soft with a net line and two white dots. Pale sky. No scoreboard, no boards, nothing readable.
scripts.hook: Luna's face close, whispering, holding a shiny crisp packet up beside her cheek like something smuggled in. Behind her Timo's narrowed eyes are fixed on the packet. Far below, a small green tennis court.

lines.direction: whispered, cut off by the packet

scripts.picture: No vlog music: the hush is the sound. SHOT 1 (0.0-5.9). 0.0 Luna sunny but whispering, her free hand up with a crisp packet (shiny, plain, no writing) by her cheek: 'We're at the tennis.' Timo: eyes narrowed. 1.85 he leans to her: 'Don't open that.' 3.2 Luna guilty: 'I'm starving.' 4.15 Timo, eyes on her: 'Wait for the clapping.' JUMP CUT closer (5.9-12.6). 5.9-7.5 nobody speaks: three slow strokes of a rally far below (sound only); Luna looking down at the packet, Timo's eyes on her. 7.5 Luna guilty, to us: 'I'll do it really slowly.' 9.7 Timo pulls his head back: 'Luna, no—' 10.2-11.5 her head bows to the packet, the packet trembles: one long slow crinkle, far worse than a quick one. 11.5 the rally stops; a thousand people: 'Shhh!' Luna: caught, she ducks. 12.1 half a second frozen. CUT tighter, both faces (12.6-18.3). 12.6 Timo, eyes shut: 'I'm not with her.' 14.4 Luna turned to him: 'We have the same scarf.' (They do: the same green and cream scarf on both, side by side in the frame.) 16.9 Timo, eyes still shut: 'Coincidence.' 17.6 hold 0.7. ENDS: she looks up at him, he stands tall with his eyes shut, two identical scarves; applause finally breaks out, one second too late. 18.3 plate 2.4 s (total 20.7).
new_drawings: Background: top rows of an outdoor tennis stand, court small below
Luna's free hand holding a plain shiny crisp packet, no writing
scripts.who_wins: Timo. He was right, she is the one shushed by a thousand people, and he has the last word. On his feet at the end.
scripts.sounds: Tennis hush: a ball struck far away, one bird, a cough. The slow crinkle (10.2-11.5), then a crowd 'Shhh!'. No music until the sung name on the plate; the applause arrives at 17.8 under the hold.
scripts.why_funny: Opening it slowly is the loudest way there is, and then he disowns her in a matching scarf; everyone who has sat in the silence before a serve has held their breath over a wrapper.

scripts.title: Twenty Years
scripts.sport: baseball
scripts.place: One background: the upper deck of a ballpark on a sunny afternoon; they have turned their backs to the field to film. Over their shoulders the green diamond far below, small and soft, soft crowd in the lower tiers, and a big sky in the top third (the ball falls out of it). No scoreboard, no boards, nothing readable.
scripts.hook: Luna close and sunny. Behind her Timo stands with his eyes shut, holding a big worn baseball glove open at his chest like a man waiting for rain.

lines.text: It's not about catching. It's about being ready. You don't—
lines.direction: eyes shut, serene, a lecture; cut off
quiet, urgent, over his last words
flat, no joy showing at all

scripts.picture: SHOT 1 (0.0-3.8). 0.0 Luna sunny, to us: 'He's brought a glove.' Timo behind her with the glove open at chest height, eyes on her. 1.65 Timo: 'Twenty years.' 2.6 Luna turned to him: 'Ever caught one?' JUMP CUT closer (3.8-10.05). 3.85 Timo shuts his eyes and lectures: 'It's not about catching. It's about being ready. You don't—' Luna faces us, sunny, half listening. 4.6 a far crack of the bat; the crowd's 'ooOOH' rises. 6.6, on the word 'ready', a white ball drops out of the sky at the top of the frame and lands in his glove (five frames, a soft thup). His eyes stay shut; he goes on talking. 6.7 Luna: oh. 7.5 Luna turned to him, over his 'You don't—': 'Timo.' 8.05 Timo, eyes shut: 'I'm not finished.' 9.25 Luna: 'Your glove.' 10.05 music stops dead. CUT tighter: both faces and the glove with the ball in it (10.05-17.4). His eyes open: on us, 0.75 s. He does not look down. 10.8 Timo: 'It's in there, isn't it.' 12.8 Luna, turned to him, whisper: 'It's in there.' 14.4 after 0.4 s, Timo to the lens, the same flat face: 'I've won baseball.' 15.9 Luna sunny, to us: 'He's thrilled.' 16.7 hold 0.7. ENDS: Luna beaming, Timo dead still with his eyes on us and the white ball sitting in his glove, the crowd cheering round them. 17.4 plate 2.4 s (total 19.8).
new_drawings: Background: ballpark upper deck, field small below, big sky
Timo, same pose, near arm up holding an open worn baseball glove at chest height
A white baseball (small: it falls, then sits in the glove)
scripts.who_wins: Timo, completely: twenty years of bringing the glove pay off while he is not even looking. On his feet, ball in glove, at the end.
scripts.sounds: Ballpark bed: organ far off with no tune anyone knows, vendors' calls as murmur. Crack of the bat (4.6), rising crowd, the thup (6.6), then cheering. Her vlog music from 0.0; it stops dead at 10.05 on 'Your glove.'.
scripts.why_funny: The ball of a lifetime lands in the glove of a man with his eyes shut explaining readiness, and his joy looks exactly like his boredom; every ballpark has the fan who has brought a glove for twenty years.

scripts.title: Beat the Crowd
scripts.sport: ice hockey (the way back to the station)
scripts.place: One background: an open-air station platform at night, completely empty: wet concrete, a pale edge line, two lamps, rails going off to the right. Far behind, across dark roofs, an indoor arena glowing, two light beams above it. No signs, no boards, no clock. On its own layer for the second shot: the platform packed with soft-shaped fans in scarves and bobble hats, arms up.
scripts.hook: Luna close and beaming, her open hand up presenting the place: a station platform at night with not one person on it. Behind her Timo, eyes shut. Far away an arena glows.

lines.text: Ice hockey tip: leave early. Beat the crowd.
lines.direction: bright, a presenter sharing a secret

lines.text: Nothing happens in the last five—
lines.direction: breezy; cut off by a goal horn

scripts.picture: SHOT 1 (0.0-4.8). 0.0 Luna sunny, her open hand up showing the empty platform: 'Ice hockey tip: leave early. Beat the crowd.' Timo: eyes shut. 3.2 Timo, eyes still shut: 'It was two-two.' JUMP CUT closer (4.8-10.45). 4.85 Luna sunny, to us: 'Nothing happens in the last five—' 7.05 a goal HORN far away cuts her off, then a roar; the arena glow pulses. Luna: guilty (sideways look at him). 8.25 a second HORN, a bigger roar, the glow pulses twice. Luna: caught. 9.15 Timo opens his eyes, on her: 'That's two nothings.' WHIP (10.45; the music is gone after it). SHOT 2 (10.75-18.2), wider: the same platform, now packed behind them with soft-shaped fans bobbing and singing. Luna: caught. Timo: eyes on us, 0.75 s. 11.5 Luna guilty: '...They caught up.' 12.75 Timo, to the lens: 'And they saw the goals.' 14.75 Luna sunny again, to us: 'We were here first.' 16.6 Timo, eyes on us: 'Same train.' 17.5 hold 0.7 as train brakes squeal in. ENDS: her crooked guilty smile, his flat look into the lens, a happy crowd bouncing behind them. 18.2 plate 2.4 s (total 20.6).
new_drawings: Background: empty station platform at night, arena glowing far behind
Crowd layer: the platform packed with soft-shaped fans in scarves and hats
scripts.who_wins: Timo. He wanted to stay, he was right, and he has the last word. On his feet at the end.
scripts.sounds: Night platform: wind, a far announcement with no words. Two distant goal horns with roars (7.05 and 8.25). After the whip: a muffled happy chant with no words, then train brakes. Her vlog music from 0.0; it is cut by the whip at 10.45.
scripts.why_funny: She left early to beat the crowd, the goals came while they stood on an empty platform, and the crowd arrived before the train did; every fan has heard the roar from outside.

scripts.title: Sound Carries
scripts.sport: golf
scripts.place: One background: the rope line beside a golf fairway on a bright morning: mown stripes, a far green with a plain flag and a soft ring of gallery round it, tall trees. Nothing readable.
scripts.hook: Luna close, whispering, eyes wide. Behind her Timo in a crisp white golf visor, eyes narrowed. A golf green very far away.

lines.text: He's miles away. Why are we whispering?

scripts.picture: ONE SHOT (0.0-7.9). 0.0 Luna sunny, whispering to us: 'He's miles away. Why are we whispering?' Timo in the visor, eyes narrowed. 3.0 he leans to her: 'Sound carries.' 4.2 from the far green, a tiny 'tock'. 4.8 a few hundred people, far away: 'Ohhhh.' Luna: caught, she ducks. Timo's eyes: on her. 6.1 after 0.3 s, Timo: 'That was you.' 7.3 hold 0.6: his eyes come to us, the flat look; her big worried eyes on us. ENDS on that. Plate 1.3 s (total 9.2).
new_drawings: Background: rope line by a golf fairway, green far away
Timo, same pose, wearing a white golf visor (face free)
scripts.who_wins: Timo. On his feet.
scripts.sounds: Golf hush: birds, a light breeze. A far putt, then a distant crowd groan. No music under the whispers; the sung name on the plate.
scripts.why_funny: She doubts that a whisper matters from that far, a putt is missed, and he hangs it on her; every golf crowd whispers half a mile from the ball and nobody knows why.

scripts.title: They Were Early
scripts.sport: baseball (the wave)
scripts.place: The ballpark upper deck of w1-twenty-years (one background if that film is not built): field small below, soft crowd in the tiers; the crowd strip can bob in a ripple, moved in the edit.
scripts.hook: Luna close, mouth wide, her free hand shooting up as a ripple runs through the soft crowd behind her. The place beside her, where a friend should be, is empty.

lines.text: The wave! Here it comes! WOOO!

scripts.picture: ONE SHOT (0.0-7.1). Timo is not in the frame (he is sitting). 0.0 the whoosh of a crowd wave coming closer; the ripple runs through the soft crowd. 0.2 Luna sunny, shouting: 'The wave! Here it comes! WOOO!'; her open hand shoots up from below on 'WOOO' (1.8). 2.5 the whoosh passes and fades; her hand goes down. Half a second of stillness. 3.0-3.7 Timo comes up into the frame, slowly, at an even speed, eyes shut, hands in his pockets, and stops at his full height. 3.7 he holds, alone, 0.4 s. 4.1 Luna turned to him: 'It's gone.' Music stops dead. 5.2 his eyes open, on her: 'They were early.' 6.4 hold 0.7: his eyes come to us. ENDS: Timo at full height with the flat look, Luna looking up at him. Plate 1.3 s (total 8.4).
new_drawings: None if the ballpark background of w1-twenty-years exists; otherwise that background (the crowd strip as a layer that can ripple)
scripts.who_wins: Timo. He does the wave on his own terms and it is the stadium that was wrong. On his feet at the end.
scripts.sounds: Ballpark crowd; the wave as a travelling whoosh and cheer that passes and dies. Her vlog music stops dead at 4.9, before his line.
scripts.why_funny: He stands up for the wave two seconds after it has gone and blames forty thousand people; every stand has the friend too proud for the wave.

scripts.title: Leftovers
scripts.sport: motor racing in the rain (the poncho)
scripts.place: The race-track fence of w1-safety-car under dark cloud in heavy rain: rain streaks and a wet grade added in the edit (one background if that film is not built). Nothing readable.
scripts.hook: Pouring rain. Timo in a clear plastic poncho with the hood up, flat-faced, water running off it. In front of him Luna, dry and delighted in the yellow raincoat she always wears.

lines.text: It's a bin bag with a hood.

scripts.picture: ONE SHOT (0.0-8.1), rain across the whole picture, her hair and scarf blowing. 0.0 Luna sunny, to us: 'He got a poncho!' Timo in the poncho, eyes on her. 1.65 Timo: 'It's a bin bag with a hood.' 4.4 Luna turned to him: 'You look great!' Music stops dead. 5.9 after 0.35 s his eyes come to us: 'I look like leftovers.' 7.45 hold 0.6: rain drums on the plastic. ENDS: Timo wrapped in clear plastic with the flat look into the lens, Luna turning back to us, sunny. Plate 1.3 s (total 9.4).
new_drawings: Timo, same pose, in a clear plastic rain poncho with the hood up (face free)
None for the place if the race-track background of w1-safety-car exists; otherwise that background

scripts.sounds: Heavy rain on plastic and on a grandstand roof, one engine far off. Her vlog music stops dead at 5.55 on 'You look great!'.
scripts.why_funny: She has been dressed for rain all along and he ends up wrapped in clear plastic; every outdoor fan has bought the emergency poncho and seen themselves in it.

scripts.title: Front of the Queue
scripts.sport: travel day: arriving four hours early
scripts.place: One background: the closed gates of a stadium at midday: a row of shuttered turnstiles under a concrete stand, and in front of them a long empty zig-zag of crowd barriers on bare paving. Flat white light. One pigeon. No signs, no numbers, no crest.
scripts.hook: Luna close with big worried eyes on us. Behind her Timo, upright and proud, eyes on us, and behind him a long zig-zag of crowd barriers and shuttered gates with nobody in it at all.

lines.text: Gates open at five. It's one.
lines.direction: to the camera, a quiet cry for help
at once, patient, as if it is obvious

scripts.picture: ONE SHOT (0.0-7.6). 0.0 Luna caught (big eyes on us): 'Gates open at five. It's one.' Timo: eyes on us. 2.4 Timo, not moving: 'Front of the queue.' 4.05 Luna turned to him: 'There's no queue.' Music stops dead. 5.25 Timo, eyes on her, almost at once: 'Because we're the front.' 6.85 hold 0.75: his eyes come back to us; Luna turns to the lens, caught. A pigeon coos. ENDS: the two of them at the head of an empty zig-zag, his flat proud look into the lens. Plate 1.3 s (total 8.9).
new_drawings: Background: shuttered stadium gates and an empty zig-zag of crowd barriers at midday
scripts.who_wins: Timo, by logic nobody can answer. On his feet.
scripts.sounds: Wind over empty paving, a shutter ticking, one pigeon. Her vlog music, thin, stops dead at 5.2 on 'There's no queue.'.
scripts.why_funny: He answers 'there's no queue' with the one thing that is true about it; every group has the friend who must be there four hours before the gates.

scripts.title: Ten Minutes
scripts.sport: travel day: the long way back to the station
scripts.place: One background: a long straight road at night after a game: street lamps in a row to a vanishing point, wet tarmac, soft shapes of other fans far behind, the stadium glow small on the horizon. No signs, nothing readable.
scripts.hook: Night. Luna close, reading her phone, pleased. Behind her Timo with a giant foam hand worn on his head like a hat, eyes shut, on a road that goes on for ever.

lines.text: Map says ten minutes to the station!
It said ten minutes twenty minutes ago.

scripts.picture: ONE SHOT (0.0-8.2); they have stopped to check the way. 0.0 Luna reading, her free hand up with her phone (we see its back): 'Map says ten minutes to the station!' Timo in the foam hand, eyes shut. 2.8 Timo, eyes shut: 'It said ten minutes twenty minutes ago.' 5.5 her eyes move along the line on her phone; her smile goes: oh (0.45 s). 5.95 Luna, small: '...It says eleven now.' Music stops dead. 7.5 Timo's eyes open: on us. Hold 0.7. ENDS: Luna looking down at her phone, Timo under the foam hand with the flat look into the lens, the road running away behind them. Plate 1.3 s (total 9.5).
new_drawings: Background: long straight road at night, stadium glow far behind
Timo, same pose, with a giant foam hand worn on his head (face free)
scripts.product_fact: none: the plate only (it is her map, not the planner: she says 'map')
scripts.who_wins: Timo is right; the road wins. On his feet.
scripts.sounds: Night street: far singing fading, a distant siren, wind. Her vlog music stops dead at 7.5 on 'eleven now'.
scripts.why_funny: The station that was ten minutes away for twenty minutes moves further off while she reads; every fan knows the walk back that the map keeps calling ten minutes.

scripts.title: It's Met Us
scripts.sport: travel day: planning the next trip on the platform home
scripts.place: The empty night platform of w1-beat-the-crowd (one background if that film is not built): wet concrete, two lamps, rails, nothing readable.
scripts.hook: Luna close and sunny on a night platform, her phone up in her free hand. Behind her Timo, flat-faced, with a giant foam hand on his head.

lines.text: The planner made three plans. I like 'Easy Pace'.

Timo in the foam hand, eyes on her. 3.55 Timo: ''Big Matches'.' 4.45 a 0.4 s beat: she turns to him, he looks down at her; nobody gives way. 4.85 Luna back to her phone, reading, then oh: '...There's one called 'Balanced'.' Music stops dead. 6.4 Timo's eyes come to us, 0.5 s. 6.9 Timo: 'It's met us.' 8.05 hold 0.45. ENDS: Luna sunny at her phone, Timo with the flat look into the lens. Plate 1.3 s (total 9.8). Check the three names on the real screen before the voices are made.

scripts.title: The Cup
scripts.sport: ice hockey
scripts.place: One background: inside an ice-hockey arena, seen from her phone as she stands at her seat in the lower bowl; the ice is behind the camera and never seen. Behind the two of them: rows of seats climbing away, the crowd as soft dark shapes in scarves, a rail, the upper tier and roof girders with plain banners, cold blue-white light. No scoreboard, no letters, no emblem.
scripts.hook: Luna's sunny face close to the lens (indoor hair). Right behind her Timo stands dead straight, hands in pockets, with a big paper soda cup, lid and straw, standing on his flat-top hair. His eyes are on us. Only the blink moves.

lines.text: Ice hockey! Second period, and we're winning!
lines.direction: bright, to the lens, over the crowd

lines.text: There's a cup on my head.
They scored when I put it there.
lines.direction: quick, as if that settles it

lines.text: When they scored, you weren't talking.

lines.direction: flat, to the lens, under the roar

scripts.picture: 0.0 Shot 1, usual width: Luna sunny; Timo behind her with the cup on his flat-top, eyes on us. 0.3 she talks to us, head tilting into the line. 3.1 he speaks with only his mouth (the cup must not fall). 5.45 she turns to him, looks up at the cup, back to us sunny. 8.2 'It's full': his eyes on her, heavy lids. 11.0 JUMP CUT, 20 per cent closer: two faces and the cup. 11.4 his eyes narrow (he is working something out). 12.7 eyes on her for 'you weren't talking'. 15.0 the music stops dead. Luna: caught, big eyes on us, mouth shut. Hold 0.75 s. 15.75 she turns to him, mouth just opening to argue. 16.1 goal horn and roar, a small bump of the camera: she snaps back to us, caught, lips pressed shut. 17.1 Timo leans a little toward the lens, eyes on us: 'She loves it.' END PICTURE (to 18.7): Luna with her mouth shut tight and her eyes sliding sideways to him (guilty face, closed crooked smile); Timo upright, the cup still on his head, looking into the lens. Then the plate, 2.4 s, over the live shot (21.1 s in all).

scripts.title: His Mother's Look
scripts.sport: basketball
scripts.place: One background: a basketball arena seen from her phone, which is on the court side. They stand in the first rows right behind the basket, so the basket and the shooter are behind the camera and never seen. Behind them: steep rows of fans as soft shapes, many waving long white balloons and foam sticks in a blur, warm arena light, a dark roof with plain banners. Nothing readable.
scripts.hook: Luna close, mouth open in a happy shout, shaking a big blank foam finger so hard it blurs. Behind her a whole stand is waving things. In the middle of it Timo stands perfectly still, hands in pockets, looking straight over the phone.

The planner says nothing about weather here: Timo only holds Luna to the planner's standard.

scripts.why_funny: Timo audits Luna's 'it'll pass' the way the planner labels every match (source, check date, status) and the sky answers for her; anyone who has sat through a rain delay has stood next to the friend who is sure it will pass.
scripts.sounds: Rain on plastic seats and on his poncho all through. Her vlog music under both shots until one clap of thunder at 12.6 cuts it dead; only rain under the last two lines. The sung name on the plate.

scripts.sounds: Afternoon: birds, a ball rattling down a metal pipe, voices far off. Dusk: fewer voices. Night: crickets, the bulbs humming. Music under line 1; it stops dead on 'I won.' One effect: a bunch of keys jingling somewhere off screen in the night shot, just before 'they're closing'.
scripts.why_funny: The sunny one turns out to be the friend who cannot lose at mini golf, and when he hands her the win she refuses it ('I want it earned'); every trip has a free afternoon that one person turns into a final.

(2) A tram platform in flat daylight: a shelter, rails, soft shapes waiting. It is used bright for day two and graded cold, grey and earlier in the morning for day three. No boards, no words.
scripts.hook: Luna shouting happily into the lens at night, her open hand in the air, the lights of an arena behind; Timo behind her with his eyes shut against the volume. The caption says 'Day one!', so a day three is coming.

lines.text: Day one! It made three plans. I picked 'Big Matches'!

lines.direction: to him, laughing at the idea
less air in her; a pause after 'Day two'; an honest question

lines.text: Day three. Is it too late for 'Easy Pace'?

lines.direction: to the lens: her words, his tone

lines.text: I'm a bit here to nap.

Timo's eyes are shut at her volume, then on her for his line, leaning a little. She answers turned to him. WHIP. SHOT 2 (8.25 to 11.7) closer, the tram platform in daylight, no hand in frame. Luna looking down on 'Day two.', then up at us, caught, for 'Who picked this?'. Timo, eyes on her: 'You. Loudly.' WHIP, and the music stops dead with it. scripts.sounds: Day one: a crowd outside an arena, a drum somewhere. Day two: a tram bell, platform murmur. Day three: the same platform almost silent, one pigeon, a tram far off. Music under days one and two; it stops dead on the whip into day three. One effect: the whip whoosh on each change of day.
scripts.why_funny: On day one she laughs at the plan called 'Easy Pace', on day three she asks for it and gets her own line back; anyone who has done three games in three days knows the exact morning it happens.

scripts.title: Tell No One
scripts.sport: rugby (the wave)
scripts.place: One background: inside a full rugby stand in daylight. They stand in a row with the crowd banked up behind them as soft shapes in mixed colours. No boards, no words.
scripts.hook: Luna's open hand shoots up, her mouth wide with joy, as a ripple of raised arms sweeps across the crowd behind her. Timo stands in the middle of it like a post, hands in his pockets.
scripts.picture: ONE SHOT (0 to 8.4), medium. A ripple of raised arms sweeps left to right across the crowd behind them; Luna's open hand flies up from below, sunny, on her line. Timo, eyes on her, does not move: 'I don't do the wave.' Half a second of stillness. The roar comes back from the other side; Luna turns her head to him. The music drops out. Timo shuts his eyes and sinks straight down out of the frame (0.7 s, even speed), hands in pockets, and as the ripple of arms passes behind where he stood he comes straight up again the same way (0.7 s), eyes still shut. He has done the wave. His eyes open onto us: flat look, 0.75 s. 'Tell no one.' ENDS: Luna turned to him, sunny, her hand still up; Timo upright, looking into the lens. Then the plate, 1.3 s (not counted).
new_drawings: background: a full rugby stand, the crowd as soft shapes
overlay: the same crowd with arms up, wiped across in the edit to make the wave
scripts.who_wins: The wave. Timo keeps his dignity by ordering a cover-up, and he is on his feet at the end.
scripts.sounds: A rugby crowd; the wave as a rolling 'whoooOOOaaa' that passes left to right, then returns right to left. Music under the first two lines; it drops out as Timo starts to sink. Silence under 'Tell no one.'
scripts.why_funny: The man who is above the wave does it anyway, eyes shut, as one straight bob with his hands in his pockets, then swears a posted video to silence; every stand has the friend who 'doesn't do the wave'.

scripts.title: It Is Nicer
scripts.sport: basketball (the friend who gets the other team's scarf)
scripts.place: One background: a street outside an indoor arena on game night. Warm doors, wet paving, and every soft shape in the crowd wearing the same dark green and cream as Luna's and Timo's scarves. A scarf stall is a blur of colour at one edge. No boards, no words, no emblem.
scripts.hook: Luna proudly holds up a beautiful sky-blue-and-gold scarf. She, Timo and every shape behind them are in dark green and cream.

lines.text: Basketball night! Look what I got!
It is nicer. Put it away.

scripts.picture: ONE SHOT (0 to 8.7), medium. From the first frame the sky-blue-and-gold scarf is up in her free hand; Luna sunny, hair blowing. Timo, eyes on her (on the scarf), leans a little: 'That's the other team's.' Luna turns to him: 'It's nicer.' The music stops dead. 0.4 s of air; his eyes go narrowed while he weighs it, then back on her: 'It is nicer. Put it away.' Half a second of stillness. The scarf sinks slowly out of the bottom of the frame (0.7 s). Luna: guilty, a sideways look at him. Timo's eyes go to us. ENDS on his flat look and her crooked smile, the green-and-cream crowd behind. Then the plate, 1.3 s (not counted).
new_drawings: background: the street outside the arena on game night, the crowd in dark green and cream
in her hand: a sky-blue-and-gold scarf held in her fist, no emblem
scripts.who_wins: Timo: he is honest enough to agree and still gets the scarf put away.
scripts.sounds: Street before a game: chatter, a home chant with a drum some way off. Music under; it stops dead on 'It's nicer.' One effect: the chant swelling a little as the scarf goes down.
scripts.why_funny: He does not argue with her taste, only with her loyalty ('It is nicer. Put it away.'); every away trip has the friend who picks the scarf by colour.

scripts.sport: American football (the last two minutes)

lines.direction: no mercy, no change of tone

WHIP: the music and the sun go together. SHOT 2 (3.5 to 7.3) closer, the same stand at night under floodlights. Luna's eyes come up to the lens: caught. Held 0.75 s. ENDS on her big worried eyes on us and Timo standing behind her exactly as he stood in daylight. Then the plate, 1.3 s (not counted).

scripts.title: They're Reloading

scripts.place: One background: the ballpark of w4-just-the-stadium, seen from the top walkway in late-afternoon light (nothing new to paint if that sketch is made first). No boards, no words.
scripts.hook: Luna waving her open hand high and shouting past the lens at something we cannot see; Timo stands behind her, unmoved. The caption reads 'I never get the free shirt!'

lines.text: Over here! I never get the free shirt!

lines.direction: eyes past the lens again, urgent

scripts.picture: ONE SHOT (0 to 8.6), medium. Luna sunny, her open hand up and waving from the first frame, calling past the lens. Timo, eyes on her. At 3.0 an air cannon thumps off screen; a rolled T-shirt drops in from the top of the frame, lands on Timo's flat-top, squashes once and stays there. He does not move at all. The music stops dead. His eyes go to us: 0.75 s. Luna has not seen it: her hand comes down, she turns to the lens, sunny but wistful: 'Eleven games. Never once.' Timo, eyes on her: 'Luna.' scripts.title: It Was an Emergency

lines.text: Timo got a poncho at the race! How much?
lines.direction: delighted, turning to him on the question

She tilts into her line and turns to him on 'How much?'. His eyes go to her: 'Luna.' The music stops. She stays turned to him: 'Roughly.' 0.45 s of air; the rain is loud on his hood. His eyes come back to the lens: 'It was an emergency.' Luna turns to us, sunny. An engine howls past behind them. ENDS: her smile, his look, the poncho shining with rain. Then the plate, 1.3 s (not counted).

Timo wearing a thin clear rain poncho with the hood up over his flat-top, face free
scripts.who_wins: Luna, by one word ('Roughly.'). Timo pays, as usual, and stands there with his dignity and his poncho.

scripts.title: Four Minutes Behind
scripts.sport: travel day (the friend who plans every minute)
scripts.place: One background: the tram platform of w4-easy-pace in flat daylight, a shelter, rails, soft shapes waiting (nothing new to paint if that sketch is made first). No boards, no words.
scripts.hook: Luna sunny on a platform; behind her Timo with a stopwatch hanging on a cord round his neck, eyes narrowed. A man timing something.

lines.text: Travel day! Timo's planned every minute.

lines.direction: flat, to the lens; a held beat and a glance down before 'Five now.'

Timo, the stopwatch on his chest, eyes narrowed, then on her as he leans a little: 'We're four minutes behind.' Luna turns to him: 'Why? What happened?' The music stops dead. 0.4 s of air. Timo's eyes come to the lens, flat look: 'This video.' Held 0.7 s; Luna's head comes round to us: caught. His eyes drop (his eyes-on-her look, here toward the stopwatch) and return to the lens: 'Five now.' ENDS: Luna caught, big eyes on us, mouth shut; Timo upright, looking into the lens. Then the plate, 1.3 s (not counted).

scripts.sounds: A platform: a tannoy mumbling far off with no words to make out, wheels, pigeons. Music under; it stops dead on 'What happened?' One effect: a stopwatch click just before 'Five now.'
scripts.why_funny: The reason the minute-by-minute plan is behind is the vlog itself, and his look into the lens is a look at the culprit; every trip has one friend with the schedule and one friend filming it.

ideas.what: A four-second loop of the two with nothing said: he looks flat at us while she steals looks at him, or his finger slowly rises beside her. On it sits a single poll, quiz or question box, and the answers feed next week's reply clips.
ideas.where_it_goes: Story, three or four a week; the best answers move into the highlight “ask Timo”.
ideas.how_made: Four loops rendered by the kit from drawings that exist (her wind and blink drawings, his wind, look, narrow and blink drawings, the finger, her phone), no captions, each ending on the frame it starts on; the hill wind as sound. Stickers are the platform's own and are typed by hand when posting. I left out a loop of him lying on the ridge on purpose: the only Black character should not be the page's wallpaper face down. Nothing new.
examples: LOOP 1 “The look” · 4 s · the two-shot; Timo looks flat into the lens; every two seconds Luna gives him a sideways look.
LOOP 2 “One question” · 4 s · Luna looks down beside her; his finger rises from below the frame, wags twice, tips over and sinks.
LOOP 3 “Reading” · 4 s · Luna reads her phone, eyes moving along the line, pleased; behind her Timo with one brow down.
LOOP 4 “The wind” · 4 s · the wider shot; Luna beams at us, hair and scarf blowing; Timo stands behind her, eyes on her, and blinks once.
On loop 4, poll: “A hike on a football trip?” · obviously / why
On loop 3, question box: “What's the worst thing a friend ever added to your trip?”
On loop 1, poll: “Who plans your trips?” · me / I find out on the day
On loop 2, quiz: “What time is the run?” · tomorrow morning (right) / never / he loves it
On loop 3, poll: “Stadium food” · part of the trip / a queue

Polls in which his answer is the sensible one teach the audience to side against Luna every time. “Next trip” is a promise: only run it when a sketch in the winning sport can really be made. Nothing here can schedule stickers; they are placed by hand.

ideas.name: The Switch, cut three more ways
