Run.”, he sinks), an opener that ends on “It said ‘hikes’”, and a 6-second bumper that is only “It was a switch!”, his look and the plate. The same drawings and voices, three more uploads.
ideas.where_it_goes: Feed post a week after the full film (cut A), story, and ad: cuts B and C are the short paid formats.
ideas.how_made: From the two finished masters in /home/user/NEXOR-PADEL/venuvoy-ads/ads/20-sketches/ (9:16 and 4:5). The plate is the film's own last 2.3 s. The music was mixed to stop on his look, so the sound of each cut is laid again from the kit's sound plan (free) instead of slicing the file. Nothing new is drawn or spoken.
examples: CUT A “What else did you flip?” · 11.1 s · film 15.9 to the end as it stands. TIMO: “...What else did you flip?” LUNA (reading): “Tomorrow morning. Run.” He shuts his eyes and sinks; thud. TIMO's finger: “Flip it back.” LUNA: “He loves it.” Plate. Caption: he asked. Pinned: I regret asking. — Timo

CUT B “Day two” · 9.3 s · film 0.0–8.0, then a 1.3 s plate. LUNA: “Day two of the football trip!” TIMO (face down behind her): “Why is there a mountain in the football trip?” LUNA: “The planner had a switch. It said ‘hikes’.” Plate. As an ad the product fact is the last thing said.
CUT C, the bumper · 6.0 s · film 11.9–15.9, then a 2 s plate with the sung name. TIMO: “So why did you fl—” LUNA: “It was a switch!” He looks at us. Plate.
ideas.risk: It is the same film again: a follower who saw it gets nothing new, so each cut is used once, on another day and preferably on another platform or as an ad. Cut B stops before the best joke and cut C has no set-up; to a stranger “It was a switch!” may mean nothing. Three is all there is until more films exist; then every sketch should be written so that its last ten seconds stand alone.

ideas.name: Luna got him something
ideas.what: Slide one is Luna, pleased with herself; swipe, and Timo is behind her wearing one thing she got him at the ground, perfectly still, looking at us, with one dry line. He wears it with dignity and gets the last word.
ideas.where_it_goes: Feed post (two slides), one a week; each drawing also gives a three-second loop for a story.
ideas.how_made: One new drawing per piece at 2 cents, made the way the kit's build notes describe for something Timo wears (redrawn from /home/user/NEXOR-PADEL/venuvoy-ads/src/film/assets/toon/duo/art/timo_clean.webp with one change, brows, eyes and mouth left free), then free stills with the caption type. The five things are the ones the rig notes already list as cheap, so an episode can use the same drawing: whichever is made first, the other gets it for nothing.
examples: THE MEDAL (a plain finisher's medal on a ribbon over his scarf, no writing). The morning after “The Switch”. LUNA: “He did the run.” / TIMO: “Faster than her.” Caption: he loves it. Pinned: I am keeping the medal. — Timo
THE PONCHO (a clear rain poncho over the jacket, hood up over the flat-top). LUNA: “It was the last one!” / TIMO: “I wonder why.”
THE EAR DEFENDERS (motorsport). LUNA: “CAN YOU HEAR ME?” / TIMO: “No. Best present you've ever got me.”
THE SUNGLASSES (under a grey sky). LUNA: “Why the sunglasses?” / TIMO: “Nil-nil. I'm asleep.”
THE FOAM HAND (a giant foam hand, worn on his head). LUNA: “Wave it!” / TIMO: “It's on my head. It's a hat now. Hats don't wave.”
ideas.risk: This is the idea most likely to slide into the childish register the founder rejected: a man in a foam hat is a nursery picture unless the line is dry. Luna dresses him every time, so if his line does not win he is the butt, which must not happen to the only Black character: the medal goes first, the foam hand last or not at all. A redraw can come back shifted against its reference and need a second go. The ear defenders want a track behind them and the sunglasses hide his eyes, which are half his acting.

ideas.name: The page as a show (profile, bio, covers, highlights)
ideas.what: Someone taps the name and sees a page that looks like one small series: the two faces stacked in the picture, a two-line bio in their voices, three pinned posts, and covers that all open on Luna's face with something odd behind her. Nothing on it looks like an advert until the link.
ideas.where_it_goes: Profile: picture, name, bio, pinned row, cover of every film, four highlight circles.
ideas.how_made: Profile picture and highlight circles from the calm-hair Luna and the clean Timo that already exist (the duo art folder), on the brand's racing green (#1e4d38). Covers are a free still of each film's first second with the title in the film's caption type, kept inside the square middle of the frame so the grid crop does not cut it. Words only otherwise. The link and the account name are still missing in the posting kit and must be filled in first.
examples: PROFILE PICTURE: a circle on racing green; her face low and sunny, his face above hers, eyes on us.
NAME: Luna & Timo · Venuvoy. BIO: Luna plans the sports trips. Timo finds out on the day. / Venuvoy: a sports-trip planner. Planning is free. / (link)
COVERS, one title each in white caption type, low in the frame: THE SWITCH · THIS IS US · HOW TO READ TIMO · WHAT ELSE DID YOU FLIP? Stills get no cover: slide one is the cover.
HIGHLIGHTS, four circles, one drawn face each: “the two” (her sunny face) · “trips” (her reading face) · “he said” (his look at us) · “ask Timo” (his finger).
PINNED ROW, left to right: “This is us” · the most-watched sketch so far · “How to read Timo”. Changed on the first of each month.
ideas.risk: Nobody shares a bio or a cover: this earns nothing by itself and only helps a person who has already come to the page. Titles on covers put words on the grid that the films themselves avoid. “Planning is free” is true, but editing and tracking a trip are paid once per trip, so the bio must never grow into “free”. Without the real link the whole page points nowhere.

ideas.name: The month, day by day
ideas.what: A 28-day plan in which no two days in a row carry the same kind of post: a film on Monday and Thursday, a short or a still between them, a swipe post on Saturday, replies on Sunday. About 48 uploads from eight sketches, four shorts and the pieces above.
ideas.where_it_goes: The posting calendar for every platform: 9:16 files to the short-video feeds, 4:5 files to the photo feeds, stories beside them.
ideas.how_made: Words only. It counts on eight sketches (“The Switch” and seven new) and four shorts from the episode batch, and on the pieces in this list. Each post gets Luna's caption and Timo's pinned comment, and the platform's label for generated content is switched on wherever it is offered, as the posting kit already says.
examples: WEEK 1 · Mon: set the profile; post and pin “This is us”; story loop 4 with “new here. I plan the trips.” · Tue: sketch 1 “The Switch”; story poll “A hike on a football trip?” · Wed: still “It's walkable.” · Thu: sketch 2; story “new one's up.” · Fri: still “We'll feel it out”; story question box “worst thing a friend ever added to your trip?” · Sat: carousel “Meet the two” · Sun: two reply clips (CUT 3 “He loves it.”, NEW 1 “what is this?”).

WEEK 2 · Mon: sketch 3 · Tue: still, the scarf · Wed: short 1 · Thu: sketch 4 · Fri: carousel “How to read Timo”; story “Ask Timo one question.” · Sat: cut A “What else did you flip?” · Sun: three reply clips and his typed answers in stories.

WEEK 3 · Mon: sketch 5 · Tue: still “Big Matches / Easy Pace” · Wed: short 2 · Thu: sketch 6 · Fri: the “Range” image; story poll “Next trip: basketball / motorsport” · Sat: carousel “How to read Luna” · Sun: reply clips.

WEEK 4 · Mon: sketch 7 · Tue: still “Extra time / Our train.” · Wed: short 3 · Thu: sketch 8 · Fri: still “rest day ... a run” and the medal; story poll “Team Luna / Team Timo” · Sat: short 4 · Sun: reply clips; story with the sport that won the vote.

RULES · never the same kind of post two days running · at most three reply clips a week · one post in four says what the product does, the rest only carry the plate · every new background or drawing an episode pays for comes back the next week as two stills and one reply clip · after two weeks, reorder by what was watched to the end.
ideas.risk: It stands on eight sketches and four shorts being finished before day one: with only “The Switch” done, the Monday and Thursday posts of weeks two to four do not exist and the month falls back on stills. Daily posting with a pinned comment and a sticker is about twenty minutes of a person's hands every day; nothing here automates it. The days are convention, not evidence: there are no numbers yet for this account.

ideas.name: "One sentence." (Timo gets one sentence to explain the sport they are standing at)
ideas.what: Luna names the sport they are at and gives Timo one sentence to explain it; he does it, dry and exact, and she tries to catch him out. Two seconds later the plate reads "one sentence. your sports trip, planned.", so the brand line is the last move of the game every week.
ideas.where_it_goes: Feed post, one a week on a fixed day (9:16 for TikTok, Reels and Shorts; the 4:5 cut for the Instagram and Facebook feed). The best three also work as 6 to 10 second ads, because the plate completes the joke.
ideas.how_made: The kit as it stands (/home/user/NEXOR-PADEL/venuvoy-ads/src/film/toon/vlog.py, vlog_sound.py, voices.py with the 'ldn' voices the founder has heard). Existing drawings: Luna with calm hair (work/duo/art/luna_calm2.png) or windy hair, her sunny, caught and turned faces; clean Timo (work/duo/art/timo_clean.png) with eyes on us and eyes on her; captions; the plate. Her first line is the title and is on screen as her caption: nothing is typed. New per piece: one background of the place (2 cents), four voice lines (about 4 cents for three readings and the pick), for some one bought sound (1.5 cents), one check (3 cents): about 15 cents each. The football one stands on the existing hill above the stadium (src/film/assets/toon/switch/art/bg_hill_1.webp) and needs no drawing. The tennis and race-track backgrounds are used again by ideas 2 and 7, so they are paid once. WHOLE SLATE (all nine ideas): 39 pieces for about 4.75 dollars; 25 of them need no new drawing; 13 new drawings in all (10 backgrounds, 3 things Timo wears). Nothing was created, spent or sent while writing this.
examples:
TENNIS (short, about 9 s, one shot). PLACE: the back row above a tennis court, the court top left, soft crowd shapes, sun. NEW: this background; one bought air (a hushed crowd, a ball being hit, polite clapping). No music: everybody whispers. Luna calm hair, Timo clean.
FIRST FRAME: Luna close with the big 'caught' eyes on us; Timo behind, eyes on us.
LUNA [whispering to the camera]: “Tennis. One sentence.”
TIMO [whispering, eyes on us, exact]: “Four thousand people keep quiet so two people can grunt.”
(Far off: the ball, a grunt. Her eyes slide sideways to him.)
LUNA [whispering, head turned to him]: “That can't be all of it.”
TIMO [whispering, eyes down on her]: “There's also a man on a very tall chair.”
She turns back to us, sunny. Plate 1.3 s.

MOTORSPORT (short, about 9 s, one shot). PLACE: the fence at a race track, a grey grandstand roof, blurs of colour. NEW: this background; one bought sound (one car screaming past). Existing wind, windy hair.
FIRST FRAME: Luna close, hair flat sideways, shouting; Timo behind, perfectly still, eyes on us.
LUNA [shouting over the engines]: “Motorsport! One sentence!”
TIMO [normal volume, eyes on us]: “You stand where it's loudest and find out who won when you get home.”
(The car screams past: the picture shakes, her hair whips.)
LUNA [shouting, head turned to him]: “WHAT?”
TIMO [same volume, eyes on us]: “One sentence. I'm not doing two.”
Plate 1.3 s.

BASKETBALL (short, about 10 s, one shot). PLACE: the upper tier of an indoor arena before the game, the court far below top left. NEW: this background; one bought air (arena murmur). Calm hair.
LUNA [bright, to the camera]: “Basketball. One sentence.”
TIMO [eyes on us, unhurried]: “Both teams score a hundred times, and it's settled in the last four seconds, which take half an hour.”
LUNA [head turned to him, pleased with herself]: “That was two sentences.”
TIMO [eyes on her, at once]: “There was a comma.”
(The music stops dead. He looks at us.) Plate 1.3 s.

SIX MORE, each a finished four-line short in the same shape (Luna: “<Sport>. One sentence.” then the three lines below):
BASEBALL. TIMO: “It's a picnic that keeps score.” LUNA: “When does it end?” TIMO [eyes on us]: “Nobody's ever stayed to find out.”
ICE HOCKEY. TIMO: “It's football on knives, and nobody can see the ball.” LUNA: “It's a puck.” TIMO: “You can't see that either.”
AMERICAN FOOTBALL. TIMO: “Eleven seconds of sport, and then a meeting.” LUNA: “And after the meeting?” TIMO: “Another meeting.”
RUGBY. TIMO: “You may only pass backwards, so everybody runs forwards, furious.” LUNA: “Why backwards?” TIMO: “You ask them.”
GOLF (whispered; Luna wins). TIMO: “A long quiet walk, and every four minutes somebody's disappointed.” LUNA [whispering, to the camera]: “So, this trip.” (He looks at us. No answer.)
FOOTBALL (on the existing hill, nothing new drawn; the warm one). TIMO: “Ninety minutes of complaining, and one of them is the best minute of your year.” LUNA [quiet, meaning it]: “...That's actually lovely.” TIMO: “It was an accident.”
ideas.risk: A man explaining sport to a woman is one bad reading away from patronising: it only works because she sets the dare and keeps the score, and in the golf one she beats him. If the first two still feel wrong, give Luna every second sentence. The whole piece is one sentence, so a flat reading kills it, and nobody in this pipeline can hear: a person must pick the takes. Whispered and shouted readings from the speech model are untested. The game leans on the tagline; two of the three judges threw out "One sentence, Timo." when it was a scold, and although this is a dare, the founder may hear the same thing. Each sentence teases a sport's own fans, gently. Nine pieces need eight new backgrounds.

ideas.name: "Timo reviews"
ideas.what: Luna announces what Timo is reviewing; he stands behind her wearing it or looking at it, gives three flat facts and a score out of ten. The picture in the first frame (deadpan Timo in a ridiculous thing) is the hook, and the score is the joke.
ideas.where_it_goes: Feed post, one a week on its own fixed day; the frame of Timo in the thing is also the cover picture and a story.
ideas.how_made: Existing: everything of both characters, the hill (bg_hill_1) and the shut gates (work/queue/art/bg_gates_1.png; run pack.py on the queue short so it is kept). New: one redraw of Timo's standing pose per thing he wears, face left free (2 cents each: big ear defenders, a giant foam hand sitting on his head, a clear rain poncho with the hood up), four voice lines per piece. The race-track background and the car sound are the ones from idea 1; the poncho is used again in idea 5. The foam hand needs the wider framing of the queue short (Timo at size 0.92, lower in the frame) so it stays in the picture. About 12 to 15 cents each.
examples:
THE EAR DEFENDERS (short, about 8 s, one shot; it reads perfectly with the sound off). PLACE: the race-track fence from idea 1. NEW: Timo in big orange ear defenders.
FIRST FRAME: Luna close, hair whipping, shouting; Timo behind in the ear defenders, serene, eyes on us.
LUNA [shouting over the engines, to the camera]: “Timo reviews: the ear defenders!”
(He looks at us. Nothing.)
LUNA [head turned to him, louder]: “Timo!”
(Nothing. One slow blink.)
LUNA [loudest]: “TIMO!”
TIMO [calm, normal volume, eyes on us]: “Ten.”
Plate 1.3 s.

THE FOAM HAND (short, about 9 s, one shot). PLACE: the shut gates (existing). NEW: Timo with a giant foam hand on his head.
FIRST FRAME: Luna sunny and close; behind her Timo, hands in pockets, the foam hand on his head like a crown, eyes on us.
LUNA [bright]: “Timo reviews: the foam hand.”
TIMO [eyes on us, flat]: “You can't clap in it. You can't hold anything in it. You can't get it home.”
LUNA: “Out of ten?”
TIMO [after a short beat]: “Nine. I'm not made of stone.”
Plate 1.3 s.

THE VIEW (short, about 8 s, one shot; nothing new drawn). PLACE: the existing hill, the stadium small in the haze below.
LUNA [bright, over the wind]: “Timo reviews: the view.”
TIMO [eyes on us]: “Sky. Grass. A stadium, very small.”
LUNA: “Out of ten?”
TIMO: “Four. It's a ten from inside.”
(The music stops. He keeps looking at us.) Plate 1.3 s.

THE RAIN PONCHO (short, about 9 s, one shot). PLACE: the hill under its grey sky, or the uncovered stand of idea 5. NEW: Timo in a clear poncho, hood up (shared with idea 5).
LUNA: “Timo reviews: the rain poncho.”
TIMO [eyes on us]: “It's a bag with a hood. I'm dry. I'm also in a bag.”
LUNA: “Out of ten?”
TIMO [lower, as if it could hear]: “Eight. Don't tell it.”
Plate 1.3 s.
ideas.risk: No product in the joke: the brand is only the plate. The shape (three flat facts, a score) is the hook and also the danger: by the sixth it can feel like a template, so the score must surprise each time and one in three should break the form, as the ear defenders do. Each worn thing is a new drawing that can come back with his face changed (redo once with the prompt changed, then drop the piece). 'Reviews' is a well-worn feed format; only Timo's seriousness makes it his.

ideas.name: "Luna reads the plan"
ideas.what: Luna lifts her phone, reads one line of today's plan out loud, and the line starts the argument. Timo answers with one dry fact that turns it, and in half of them he is the one who was ahead all along.
ideas.where_it_goes: Feed post, weekly, alternating with idea 4; also a story on the day a longer sketch goes up.
ideas.how_made: Nothing new is drawn. Existing: her phone hand with the reading face whose eyes move along the line (luna_read3, luna_read3b), her 'oh', looking-down, guilty and sunny faces; Timo's narrowed eyes, eyes on us, and the music stopping dead before his look; the shut gates and the hill. New: three to six voice lines per piece (about 4 cents) and the check (3 cents): about 10 cents each. Product truth used: the planner makes two or three versions with the names Big Matches, Balanced and Easy Pace; every match shows its source, the date it was checked and a status; a place to play from 'Sport nearby' is added to the plan by hand; paid tracking tells you when a game moves.
examples:
I PICKED AFTER YOU (short, about 8 s, one shot). PLACE: the existing gates or the hill.
FIRST FRAME: her phone up in her free hand, the pleased reading face; behind her Timo's eyes already narrowed.
LUNA [reading off her phone, delighted]: “‘Friday: a game. Saturday: a game. Sunday: a game.’”
TIMO [slow, eyes narrowed]: “I picked the plan called ‘Easy Pace’.”
LUNA [a sideways look at him, then sunny to the camera]: “I picked after you.”
(The music stops dead. His eyes come to us, 0.75 s.) Plate 1.3 s.

SOURCE? (short, about 9 s, one shot; Timo wins).
LUNA [reading]: “‘Sunday, four p.m.: the match.’”
TIMO [eyes on her, flat]: “Source?”
LUNA [reading on, the 'oh' face]: “...It actually says the source. And the day they checked it.”
TIMO [eyes on us, proud]: “I don't travel on a rumour.”
Plate 1.3 s.

KEEP READING (short, about 9 s, one shot; Timo is the one who added something this time).
LUNA [reading, then sunny to the camera]: “‘Thursday: free afternoon.’ Finally.”
TIMO [eyes on us]: “Keep reading.”
LUNA [reading, the 'oh' face]: “‘Three p.m.: mini golf.’ ...I didn't add that.”
TIMO [calm, eyes on us]: “I did. I'm extremely good.”
(She turns her big 'caught' eyes to us.) Plate 1.3 s.

I THOUGHT IT WAS THE WEATHER (about 12 s, one shot, six short lines). PLACE: the existing shut gates and empty queue lanes; a still day, calm hair.
FIRST FRAME: Luna's 'caught' eyes close to the lens; behind her nothing but shut gates and empty barriers; Timo's eyes on us.
TIMO [eyes on us]: “Nobody's here.”
LUNA [reading her phone, small]: “It says the game moved to Sunday.”
TIMO: “When did it say that?”
LUNA [looking down]: “Tuesday.”
TIMO [patient]: “And you saw it.”
LUNA [a guilty look at him, then sunny to the camera]: “I thought it was the weather.”
(The music stops dead. He looks at us.) Plate 1.3 s.
ideas.risk: The first frame is a woman reading her phone: the weakest hook on this list, so it must open on something odd behind her (the empty gates, his narrowed eyes) or it gets swiped. Three of the four quote the product, which is where a sketch starts to sound like an advert, and every quoted word (the plan names, the source and check date, mini golf added by hand, the message about a moved game) must be checked against the real screen before recording. The moved-game message belongs to the paid tracking: the piece must not suggest it is free or instant. The shape is the same as The Switch (she reads, he pays), so at least half must end with Timo ahead.

ideas.name: "Question." (the two of them answer what people really ask about a sports trip)
ideas.what: Luna reads one real question off her phone and they give two answers: hers cheerful and wrong, his one dry line that is right. Eight seconds, no lecture.
ideas.where_it_goes: Comment reply first (each real question under a film answered with its own eight-second film), also feed post, and a story with the platform's question box to collect the next ones.
ideas.how_made: Nothing new is drawn. Existing: her phone hand and reading face, sunny and turned faces, Timo's eyes on us and on her, his cutting-in (the kit's interruption that runs 0.2 s under her voice), any existing background. New: four voice lines (about 4 cents) and the check: about 10 cents each. Each one can be turned round in about an hour of work plus the render, which is what a comment reply needs.
examples:
ON YOUR OWN (short, about 8 s, one shot).
LUNA [reading off her phone]: “Question: ‘Is it weird to go to a game on your own?’”
TIMO [eyes on us, at once]: “No. It's the best way to go.”
LUNA [head turned to him]: “You've never been on your own.”
TIMO [eyes on her]: “I've never been allowed.”
Plate 1.3 s.

NAME THE THIRD (short, about 9 s, one shot; Timo wins).
LUNA [reading, then sunny to the camera]: “‘How many games can you fit in one weekend?’ Four!”
TIMO [eyes on us]: “Two. And you remember both.”
LUNA [head turned to him]: “We did four in a weekend.”
TIMO: “Name the third.”
(Her eyes go down, the small round 'oh'. The music stops.) Plate 1.3 s.

EVERYBODY'S COUSIN (short, about 9 s, one shot; the product is in it once).
LUNA [reading]: “‘Where do you two get your tickets?’”
TIMO [eyes on us]: “The official link. It's first in the plan.”
LUNA [bright]: “Or my cousin knows a man who—”
TIMO [cutting in, not raising his voice]: “Everybody's cousin knows a man.”
Plate 1.3 s.

JUST TURN UP (short, about 9 s, one shot; the brand is the answer without being named).
LUNA [reading, then sunny]: “‘Do you even need a plan? Can't you just turn up?’ Yes! Just turn up!”
TIMO [eyes on us]: “We just turned up once.”
LUNA: “That was a great weekend.”
TIMO: “The game was the weekend after.”
Plate 1.3 s.

IS IT REALLY ONE SENTENCE (short, about 10 s; the honest product answer). LUNA [reading]: “‘Is it really just one sentence?’” TIMO [eyes on us]: “Where, when, which sport, how many of you. Then you check it and press the button.” LUNA [sunny]: “He checks it. I press the button.” TIMO: “That is the correct order.”
MORE QUESTIONS READY TO WRITE UP THE SAME WAY: ‘How early should I get there?’ (TIMO: “Two hours.” LUNA: “What do you do for two hours?” TIMO: “Watch you not be there.”) · ‘What if I don't support either team?’ (TIMO: “Support whoever is sitting next to you. Loudly.”) · ‘Do I need the language?’ (TIMO: “You need ‘two’, ‘please’ and ‘which gate’.”)
ideas.risk: Until real questions arrive these are ours: she says "Question", never "someone asked" and never a made-up name. The format only comes alive as a reply to a real comment, and that needs someone to turn a piece round in a day. The first frame is again her phone. True answers about tickets and money are narrow (no price, no promise, nothing about fakes), so most answers have to be about people, not the product; the ticket one and the one-sentence one are the only product answers, and the last is more true than funny.

ideas.name: "He loves it." (the running gag, with rules so it does not wear out)
ideas.what: The button of The Switch comes back, never the same way twice: said by her about his misery, said by him about hers, said when it is secretly true, or forbidden before she can say it. The viewer who has seen two films starts waiting for it, and the one who has seen none still gets a joke.
ideas.where_it_goes: Inside the feed posts (at most two films in three) and as the pinned comment under every film ("he loves it."). The three below are feed posts of their own.
ideas.how_made: Existing: everything; two of the three stand on the existing hill and gates and need no drawing. New for the third: one background (an uncovered stand in the rain facing a roofed stand, 2 cents) and Timo in the clear poncho (2 cents, shared with idea 2). Rules for whoever writes the next ones: 1 straight (she says it to the lens about him); 2 reversed (he says "She loves it." when she pays); 3 true (he really does love it and will not admit it); 4 forbidden (he stops her: "Don't."); 5 silent (she breathes in, he sinks out of frame before the word). Never the same way in two films running. His flat look into the lens with the music cut stays his own signature and is not used in the same film as hers.
examples:
REVERSED: SHE LOVES IT (short, about 9 s, one shot; Timo wins; nothing new drawn). PLACE: the existing hill, wind.
FIRST FRAME: Luna's big 'caught' eyes close to the lens, hair blown flat; behind her Timo upright and perfectly fresh, eyes on us.
TIMO [eyes on us, flat, not out of breath]: “Day three of the trip. The morning run.”
LUNA [out of breath, big eyes on us]: “Nobody said it was uphill.”
TIMO [eyes down on her]: “You added it to the plan.”
(The music stops dead. His eyes come back to us.)
TIMO [to the camera, in exactly her tune]: “She loves it.”
Plate 1.3 s.

TRUE: HE IRONED THE SCARF (short, about 9 s, one shot; nothing new drawn). PLACE: the existing shut gates on a quiet morning with no game.
LUNA [low, to the camera, a sideways look at him]: “Stadium tour at ten. He's been ready since six.”
TIMO [eyes on us]: “I'm fine either way.”
LUNA: “He ironed the scarf.”
(His eyes shut.)
LUNA [sunny, to the camera]: “He loves it.”
Plate 1.3 s.

FORBIDDEN: DON'T (about 12 s, one shot, six short lines). PLACE: an uncovered stand in the rain; across the pitch, top left, a stand with a roof. NEW: that background and Timo in the clear poncho, hood up.
FIRST FRAME: Luna sunny in her yellow raincoat; behind her Timo in a bag-like poncho, eyes on us.
LUNA [bright]: “Outdoor seats! Right in the weather!”
TIMO [eyes on us]: “She picked them for the view.”
LUNA: “You can see everything!”
TIMO: “I can see the roof. It's over there. On the other side.”
LUNA [sunny, to the camera, breath in]: “He—”
TIMO [not moving]: “Don't.”
Plate 1.3 s.
ideas.risk: It is glue, not a format: it only works riding on a situation, and these three are really three ordinary shorts with the same last line. A catchphrase dies of repetition, hence the rule of two films in three. The reversed and forbidden versions are funnier for someone who has heard the straight one. The brand is not in it. With the sound off it is one more caption. The third runs six lines and costs two drawings. The stadium tour is real in the product only in England and never on a match day, so that piece must not show a crowd or name a ground.

ideas.name: "It's that week." (the sports calendar, with no competition named)
ideas.what: A short for the moments every fan's year has: the weekend with no game, the first day of the season, the day after it ends, the draw, the morning the fixtures come out. Nothing is named; the fan knows which week it is.
ideas.where_it_goes: Feed post and story on the day itself, about ten days a year; made ahead and held. Rough calendar to check each year: the opening weekend (mid August), the weekends the leagues stop (early September, mid October, mid November, late March), the day after the last game (late May), the morning the fixture list comes out (mid June), any cup draw.
ideas.how_made: Nothing new is drawn: all five stand on the existing shut gates (an empty forecourt is the picture of a weekend with no game) or the existing hill. Existing faces, phone hand, Timo's shut eyes, narrowed eyes and look at the lens. New: four or five voice lines each (about 4 cents) and the check: about 10 cents each. Sports named are only ones that really have events in the catalog.
examples:
THE WEEKEND WITH NO GAME (short, about 9 s, one shot; Timo wins; shows it is more than football). PLACE: the existing shut gates, empty lanes.
FIRST FRAME: Luna's tragic 'caught' eyes close; behind her the shut gates.
LUNA [tragic, to the camera]: “No game this weekend. Not ours. Not anybody's.”
TIMO [eyes on her]: “There's basketball. Ice hockey. Rugby. Golf.”
LUNA [head turned to him]: “You'd watch golf?”
TIMO [eyes on us]: “I'd watch you stay quiet for four hours.”
Plate 1.3 s.

THE DAY AFTER THE SEASON ENDS (short, about 9 s, one shot). PLACE: the hill or the gates.
FIRST FRAME: Luna sunny; behind her Timo standing with his eyes shut, asleep on his feet.
LUNA [low, to the camera]: “The season ended yesterday.”
TIMO [eyes shut, not moving]: “Wake me in August.”
LUNA [reading her phone]: “There's baseball all summer.”
(One beat. His eyes open, narrowed.)
TIMO: “...Where?”
Plate 1.3 s.

THE FIRST DAY OF THE SEASON (short, about 8 s, one shot; Luna wins by not listening). PLACE: the hill, the stadium below.
LUNA [sunny]: “First day of the season! We're top of the table.”
TIMO: “Nobody has played.”
LUNA: “And we're top.”
TIMO [eyes on us]: “It's alphabetical.”
(She keeps smiling at the lens. He keeps looking at us.) Plate 1.3 s.

TWO MORE, finished.
THE DRAW (about 10 s). LUNA [reading her phone, the 'oh' face]: “The draw's out. We got them away.” TIMO: “How far away?” LUNA [reading, small]: “...Far.” TIMO [eyes shut]: “It'll be a Tuesday night.” LUNA [sunny, to the camera]: “Sports trip!”
THE MORNING THE FIXTURES COME OUT (about 9 s). LUNA [reading, fast, thrilled]: “The fixtures are out! I've picked three weekends.” TIMO: “They came out four minutes ago.” LUNA: “Four good minutes.” TIMO [eyes on us]: “They'll move every one of those games.”
ideas.risk: It follows the calendar of European football, which is not every viewer's; the week cannot be named in the film or in the post text, so some viewers will not know why today. Each piece is worth posting for a few days a year and must be ready before the day, which means someone keeps a calendar. The first-day one rests on a joke fans already tell each other. The draw and the fixtures pieces have no strong picture. The fixtures piece must never suggest the product had the new games within minutes; as written she only picks weekends.

ideas.name: "What did he say?" (a sound from outside the picture, and the two of them working it out)
ideas.what: Something is heard that we never see: a loudspeaker nobody can understand, a roar from a stadium they are not in, an umpire's murmur. Luna asks what it was and Timo's answer is exact and useless.
ideas.where_it_goes: Feed post now and then (five or six exist in this idea, not fifty); best with sound on, so not for ads.
ideas.how_made: Existing: both characters, the hill with the stadium far below (the roar comes from it), the tennis background from idea 1. New: one bought sound per piece (1.5 cents; it must be heard back as what was asked for), a station platform background for the first (2 cents), four voice lines each. About 12 to 14 cents each. The rig allows a crowd, an announcer or an engine to be heard but never seen and never captioned.
examples:
THE PEOPLE IN THE STADIUM (short, about 8 s, one shot; nothing new drawn; the strongest of the three, and it works silent). PLACE: the existing hill, the stadium small and far below. NEW: one bought sound, a far crowd roar.
FIRST FRAME: Luna close, hair in the wind; behind her Timo; far below, the stadium.
(Far below: a roar.)
LUNA [head turned to him]: “Was that a goal?”
TIMO [eyes on her]: “That was a goal.”
LUNA: “Who for?”
TIMO [eyes on us]: “The people in the stadium.”
(The music stops dead. He keeps looking at us.) Plate 1.3 s.

PLATFORM (short, about 9 s, one shot). PLACE: a station platform on match day, soft shapes of people far off, no signs. NEW: this background; one bought sound, a station loudspeaker announcement that cannot be understood.
(The loudspeaker: a blur of words.)
LUNA [head turned to him]: “What did he say?”
TIMO [eyes on her]: “‘Platform.’”
LUNA: “Which platform?”
TIMO [eyes on us]: “He was very clear about the word ‘platform’.”
Plate 1.3 s.

LOVE (short, about 8 s, one shot, whispered). PLACE: the tennis back row from idea 1, its hushed air.
(Far off: an umpire's calm voice, too far to make out.)
LUNA [whispering]: “What's the score?”
TIMO [whispering]: “Forty-love.”
LUNA [whispering, head turned to him]: “Love?”
TIMO [whispering, eyes on us]: “It means nothing.”
(Her big 'caught' eyes come to the lens.) Plate 1.3 s.
ideas.risk: The trigger is a sound, so with the sound off the first second has no hook and the platform piece loses half its joke; only the hill one survives silent, because the picture explains it. A loudspeaker that is unreadable on purpose is a hard thing to ask a sound model for and may need a second try. The idea runs out after five or six pieces. Weak as a weekly format; good as an occasional one.

ideas.name: "Timo or Luna?" (one question, two kinds of sports traveller)
ideas.what: Luna asks the lens one question about how you do a sports trip and the two give opposite answers, each sure the other is mad. Nobody wins; the post text asks which one you are.
ideas.where_it_goes: Feed post with the post text "are you a timo or a luna?"; story with the platform's two-way poll. Run this or idea 4 in a given week, not both.
ideas.how_made: Nothing new is drawn. Existing characters, phone hand for the third, any existing background. New: four voice lines (about 4 cents) and the check: about 10 cents each. The third uses the planner's real plan names (Big Matches, Balanced, Easy Pace).
examples:
WHEN DO YOU LEAVE (short, about 8 s, one shot).
LUNA [to the camera]: “When do you leave a game?”
TIMO [eyes on us, at once]: “Eighty-five minutes. Beat the crowd.”
LUNA [head turned to him]: “He's missed four winning goals.”
TIMO [eyes on us]: “And not one train.”
Plate 1.3 s.

WHAT DO YOU PACK (short, about 8 s, one shot).
LUNA [to the camera]: “What do you pack for a sports trip?”
TIMO [eyes on us]: “What's on the list.”
LUNA [head turned to him]: “There's a list?”
TIMO [eyes on us]: “It's laminated.”
Plate 1.3 s.

THE THREE PLANS (short, about 10 s, one shot; the product is in it).
LUNA [reading her phone]: “It made three plans. ‘Big Matches.’” [sunny, to the camera] “Mine.”
TIMO: “‘Easy Pace.’ Mine.”
LUNA [reading]: “And ‘Balanced’.”
(Both look at the lens. One beat of silence.)
TIMO [eyes on us]: “That one's for people who agree.”
Plate 1.3 s.
ideas.risk: 'Two kinds of people' is the most worn template on any feed, and with no winner the jokes are softer than the rest of this list. It overlaps with idea 4. The third laughs at one of the product's own three plans; the founder should see that line before it is recorded. The real value is in the replies ("I'm a Timo"), which cannot be judged on paper. Weak unless the comments take it up.

ideas.name: The trailers: who these two are, in 15 seconds, 6 seconds, and a cut of what exists
ideas.what: One short film that introduces the pair as a joke and sits pinned on the profile, a six-second version for paid placement, and a cut made only from films that already exist. The viewer who lands on the profile knows in a quarter of a minute what this is and that there is more.
ideas.where_it_goes: Profile and pinned (the 15-second one); ad (the six-second one); feed post and story about once a month (the cut of existing films).
ideas.how_made: The 15-second one uses only existing drawings on the existing hill: its first frame is the first frame of The Switch (Luna close, Timo face down on the slope behind her, the drawing timo_prone_1 with prone_wind1 and prone_wind2), then the upright two-shot; new are seven voice lines (about 8 cents) and the check. The six-second one is one shot on the same hill, two new lines. The third costs nothing: it is cut with ffmpeg from the finished films' own frames and lines (/home/user/NEXOR-PADEL/venuvoy-ads/ads/20-sketches/venuvoy-sketch-01-the-switch-en_9x16_1080x1920.mp4 and the queue short when it is finished), ending on the existing plate with the sung name.
examples:
THE PROFILE TRAILER (about 16 s, two shots, seven lines). PLACE: the existing hill.
FIRST FRAME: Luna close, hair blown flat; far behind her on the slope Timo lies face down in his scarf.
LUNA [bright, to the camera]: “Hi! I'm Luna. This is my sports trip vlog.”
TIMO [from the grass, muffled; he lifts his head a little]: “I'm also on the trip.”
JUMP CUT, closer. Timo upright behind her, a blade of grass on his cheek.
LUNA [sunny]: “That's Timo. He likes a plan. I like a surprise.”
TIMO [eyes on us]: “She puts the surprises in the plan.”
LUNA: “New trip every week. Tennis, motorsport, baseball—”
TIMO [cutting in, eyes on her]: “Hills.”
LUNA [sunny, to the camera]: “He loves it.”
(The music stops dead. He looks at us, 0.75 s.) Plate 2.4 s with the sung name.

THE SIX-SECOND AD (one shot, two lines). PLACE: the existing hill.
FIRST FRAME: Luna sunny and close; Timo behind, eyes on us.
LUNA [sunny]: “One sentence. That's how this sports trip started.”
TIMO [eyes on us, flat]: “It's day four. It hasn't stopped.”
Plate 1.3 s.

THE TRIP SO FAR (about 12 s, no new drawing, no new voice). Only Timo's lines, back to back, each in its own frame from its own film, then Luna once.
TIMO: “Why is there a mountain in the football trip?” (The Switch, first shot)
TIMO: “Front of the queue.” (the queue short)
TIMO: “What else did you flip?” (The Switch, third shot)
TIMO: “Because we're the front.” (the queue short)
TIMO: “Flip it back.” (The Switch, his raised finger)
LUNA: “He loves it.” (The Switch)
Plate 2.4 s with the sung name. Made again each month from whatever has been finished since.
ideas.risk: Low volume by nature: three pieces, not a weekly format. Nobody shares a trailer; its job is the pinned place and paid placement. The first has to say who they are, and explaining is exactly what the founder rejected, so every line of it must also be a joke; it is the longest thing on this list. The six-second one shortens "the sentence fills the planner and you press Create plans" to "one sentence", the same shortcut the sign-off already takes. The cut of existing films is thin with two films and only good from five; its captions are burned into the source frames, so every cut must fall between lines, and the queue short is not finished yet.

scores.note: "I have a pillar." is a line a person says, the swap is one clean turn, and "You'd have loved it." is the right last beat. Post it well apart from At the Nachos, which ends on the same withholding.

Her logic gets stronger with every line and his surrender, "...Come on, safety car.", is the funniest beat and the last one. It is the motorsport pick joke to keep; The Yellow One is the same idea done weaker.

Everyone has opened a packet slowly and made it worse, and "I'm not with her." / "We have the same scarf." / "Coincidence." is the best closing run in the set. Give the crowd's "Shhh!" a jolt of the picture so the turn reads with the sound off.
The ball lands while he lectures on readiness with his eyes shut: it reads silent and Timo wins. "I've won baseball." is the peak and "He's thrilled." is a fair tag.
Good shape and "Same train." is a proper ending. Optional lift: between the two horns Luna says, small, "Could be a fight." (saved from The Only Goal, which is this same joke).
"That was you." is unfair in exactly the right way. Same family as Really Slowly (Luna against a silent crowd), so weeks apart; the visor adds nothing and can go.
The slow rise after the wave has gone is the best physical joke the rig has, and "They were early." is pure Timo. This is the one wave piece to make.
"I look like leftovers." is the best last line of the poncho shorts. The idea 'Timo reviews: the rain poncho' repeats its bag-with-a-hood line; say it here only.
Clean four lines, logic nobody can answer, and the empty zig-zag stops a thumb. The same exchange is repeated inside Don't Wave Back: it belongs here.
"It said ten minutes twenty minutes ago." is how people talk and eleven is the right topper. The foam hand does nothing for the joke; plain Timo is enough.

"It's met us." is a good product line, but the picks contradict Easy Pace and the ideas. Swap them: LUNA: "The planner made three plans. I like 'Big Matches'." TIMO: "'Easy Pace'." (rest unchanged; drop the foam hand).
Her superstition turned on her, then the horn proving him right while her mouth is shut, is real construction and the cup on his head is a hook. Cut the "Nothing." / "Nothing!" echo if it runs long.

Best in the set: "Sorry! ...What did I do?" / "Exactly.", then his look goes down the lens at us and the shot misses. "He knows what he did." is the funniest last line here; trim the three-sentence opener to two.
"Gary has a grill." / "He's invited me for Thanksgiving." / "It's a family thing.": the reversal is complete and each line tops the one before. Nothing else in the set is like it.
Picking by colour and winning is an old joke, and Safety Car does 'her logic beats his expertise' better on the same track. Bank "Strategically." for another day.

"The windmill has a rhythm." and "Let them watch." are good, but the putt is heard and not seen, so a silent viewer loses the turn. Make it after Best of Three and weeks apart: same course, same opening line.
Costs nothing, needs no context, and "Okay. Too much." is last and funniest. The kind people send with 'this is you'.
The film dying in the middle of the word is the joke, and nobody has to explain it. Top short.
Quick and true, and "You were at the nachos." lands. It is the third 'she missed it' piece after The Pillar and Beat the Crowd, so post it far from both.
The see-saw is neat but "Someone has to." needs a second of thought, and it is the weakest of three wave pieces.
A pun on a plan name with Timo as the target, and "I'm Easy Pace." is not something a person says. Fourth plan-name piece and the weakest.
"You wear it every day." / "And today I'm right." is a joke about her that she wins, which the set needs. Not in the same fortnight as Leftovers.

"Source?" as the answer to "It'll pass." is good and "...Provisional." under thunder is a real ending, but line six is the fact sheet talking. New line: TIMO: "The plan gives every match a source, a date and a status. I'd like yours."

"Official Dave." / "It's in his name!" and "He says hurry." are the best product jokes written so far, and "Bye, Dave." is a warm button. The sport is free to change, since ice hockey already has The Cup and Beat the Crowd.

As written the joke is only that she forgot, it contradicts the woman who flips every switch, and it shows the tagline failing just before the plate. New line nine: LUNA: "I was saving it for today!" (her taste for surprises, not forgetfulness); make it late in the run.

"Nothing blocks you." is the laugh and "LAP. YOU." over the engine is a strong finish with Timo keen for once. Keep the ear-defender insult here only: the still 'Best present you've ever got me' is the same joke.

"I thought you meant emotionally!" and then "They were good fixtures." / "He printed them." is a lovely run, with Timo right and teased fondly. The idea 'I thought it was the weather' is the same wrong-day joke: drop that one.
"He doesn't have a link. He has a coat." is a clean one-turn short. Companion to Official Dave, so weeks apart.
Tiny rigid Timo crossing the sky twice is the best silent joke among the shorts, and "Again." turns it. Nobody says the feature name aloud: LUNA: "Free afternoon! I added a zipline to the plan."
Warm and funny: the roar in his head cuts out on "Timo." and "...We won." pays it. It shows he loves it without anyone saying the catchphrase.
A grammar joke about how the product is fed: a stranger does not know which sentence or which planner, and her first line is a list no person would say.
"I hate it less than you." is spite as a travel plan and works for someone who never saw The Switch. Timo wins outright.
An old shape done well: the air before "To three." is the joke and it is last. Third plan-name piece, so keep it away from Easy Pace and It's Met Us.

The sun-hat rival and the frozen hand that waves once more are wonderful, but lines two to four are Front of the Queue again. Cut "Queues." / "There was no queue." / "Because we're early." and go from "It's nine." to "Well, at least we're first." / "Second."; after "Every year." add LUNA: "What time does he get here?" TIMO: "I've never found out."

Two jokes held by one sentence: the foam-hand cut is the first laugh and "No idea. I'm in your video." is the better one and rightly last. "I have a mortgage." is the adult register that was asked for.

Funny lines, but it is Beat the Crowd again (nothing will happen, horn) in the same sport, with At the Nachos' tray, and "Nacho?" is a soft last beat. Move "Could be a fight." into Beat the Crowd and drop the rest.

Luna gets a new adult flaw, she cannot lose, and "They can close around us." / "I don't want it given! I want it earned!" / "Help." climbs to the end. One painting in three lights is a cheap time joke that reads silent.

Best product sketch: he hands back "We're not here to nap." and "I'm a bit here to nap." is the right last line. For a stranger 'It' has no owner: LUNA: "Day one! The planner made three plans. I picked 'Big Matches'!"
A decent joke ("Tell no one." said into a camera) but it is the same sink-and-rise wave as They Were Early, which is better. Bank it for a later month.
"It is nicer. Put it away." is honest, quick, and the picture alone tells it: one blue scarf in a street of green.

True of the sport and told by the light going from gold to night; "A minute fifty." is the whole joke and it is last. The 'One sentence' basketball line about the last four seconds is the same joke: keep this one.
The shirt lands on the man who never asked, she never sees it, and "Not now. They're reloading." is perfect. With Four Percent, the top two shorts.
"Roughly." is the best single word in the set and stadium prices are a truth everyone knows. It is the third poncho short: a month from Leftovers.
The proof is the video we are watching, and "Five now." tops it. A good cheap short.

verdicts.overall: A strong batch whose problem is sameness, not quality. The same joke comes back: the wave three times, the missed goal four, the poncho four, the plan names four, the empty ground three. One of each, or a month apart. Thirty-nine of 44 end on Timo's look down the lens; end a third on Luna, a picture or black. Timo wears something in nearly half the pieces: drop it where it is not the joke. Fix who is who: Luna picks 'Big Matches', Timo 'Easy Pace'; decide who leaves early. Missing: football, and a picture cue for every off-screen horn or groan. Of the ideas, skip the re-cuts, the story loops and the second pinned trailer.

scores.note: A restricted-view seat is something every fan knows, half a face behind a pillar stops the thumb, and "You'd have loved it." is dry and kind at once. Rugby, no product, Timo wins standing.
One joke that climbs, and Timo changing sides with a flat "Come on, safety car." is exactly eye level. Keep it as the only 'Luna picks the wrong car' piece; it replaces The Yellow One.
The slow crisp packet in a tennis hush is universal and plays with the sound off; "We have the same scarf." / "Coincidence." is a line people repeat. A human ear must pass the whispered voices.
The best of the batch: a proud man, a lecture, and the ball lands while his eyes are shut. "I've won baseball." / "He's thrilled." is warm, adult and all Timo's.
"That's two nothings." and "Same train." are real laughs, and it is about the travel, not only the game. Keep Luna as the early leaver everywhere: one content idea gives that habit to Timo.
Eight seconds, one clean turn, golf. Not in the same fortnight as Really Slowly, which is the same hush joke.
The best of the three wave shorts: he rises alone after it has passed and blames the stadium. Make only this one.
"I look like leftovers." is a good line, but this is the third poncho short and Timo only suffers in it. Keep the line in reserve; It Was an Emergency and Rain Delay cover the poncho.
Logic nobody can answer in seven seconds, and the picture reads silent. It is the reason Don't Wave Back must lose its two repeated lines.
Every fan has walked this road, and "It said ten minutes twenty minutes ago." is how a tired friend says it. Keep the word 'map' so nobody thinks the planner was wrong.

"It's met us." is the best of the plan-name jokes, but the names are the wrong way round for these two and for Easy Pace. New lines: LUNA "The planner made three plans. I like 'Big Matches'." TIMO "'Easy Pace'."; and drop the foam hand, it does nothing here.

A joke about the product's own extra step: only the people who wrote the rules will laugh, Luna looks dim for three weeks, and the planner comes across as a chore. Drop.
"Nothing blocks you." and "LAP. YOU." are good, and he wants the karting, which is warm. Replace the menu-sounding line with: "So. Secret. I added karting to the plan."

"I thought you meant emotionally!" / "Matches don't move me." / "He printed them." is two real friends teasing, with the alert doing its job quietly. Not next to the queue short, which has the same empty gates.
"He doesn't have a link. He has a coat." Nine seconds, and the product is the set-up, not the pitch. One tout piece per fortnight; Official Dave is the other.
A tiny rigid Timo sliding across the sky and coming back for more is charming and looks like nothing else in the set. Line 1 without the menu name: "Free afternoon! I added a zipline to the plan."
Every fan has done this on a stadium tour, and it is the one piece where he is caught being happy. The set needs this warmth.
A grammar joke about the slogan is writers' room humour, and "It filled in the planner!" is copy. Drop.
"I hate it less than you." is the sharpest thing a friend can say, and it turns The Switch round with him winning. It stands alone.
"I've narrowed it down. To three." is a clean small joke anyone gets. Second month: the three plans already have Easy Pace and It's Met Us.

The rival in the sun hat ("Every year." / "Don't wave back.") is lovely, and her frozen hand waving once more is a real ending. Cut "There was no queue." / "Because we're early.", which repeat the existing queue short; go from "Queues." straight to "Well, at least we're first."

"I have a mortgage." and "No idea. I'm in your video." are grown-up laughs about merchandise and about filming instead of looking. It is two jokes, not one, which puts it just outside the first eight.
"Could be a fight." / "That was a goal." / "Nacho?" is tight and true. Same sport and same loss as Beat the Crowd, so three weeks apart.

"They can close around us." is excellent, but it is a second mini-golf sketch beside The Windmill. Move it to bowling, which is in the same product list: "Free afternoon! I added bowling to the plan.", with the lanes going dark instead of dusk; otherwise hold it for month two.
Day one loud, day three hoarse, and he beats her with her own sentence: "We're not here to nap." / "I'm a bit here to nap." The product is inside the joke and nobody explains it.
Sweet, but it is a second wave short, and sinking out of the frame reads as ducking, not joining in. Hold; They Were Early is the wave.
"It is nicer. Put it away." is an honest man in five words, and the colours tell it with the sound off. The best short.
Day to night in one cut, then "A minute fifty.": true, quick, and exactly a visitor's first American football game.

The shirt lands on the man who never asked while she begs for one, and it is funny silent. No line changes: stage it in the basketball arena, so it is not the second 'something drops on Timo at the ballpark' after Twenty Years.
"How much?" / "Luna." / "Roughly." Everyone has paid that price for that poncho, and Luna wins by one word. This is the poncho short to make.
"This video. Five now." The joke is the film we are watching: grown-up and very him.

verdicts.overall: 36 of 44 are worth making. Repeats: three wave shorts, four ponchos, five pieces on the three plans, four missed goals, three early arrivals, two mini golfs, two 'Luna picks a car'. One of each per month. Watch: nearly every piece hooks on Timo in a silly hat and ends on music-stop plus his look; a hat only when it is the joke, or it drifts childish. Character slips: Timo is Easy Pace; the idea where Timo leaves at eighty-five minutes contradicts Beat the Crowd. Lacks: being abroad (language, local habits), a golf sketch, moments of plain enjoyment. Ideas: cut the 'Love?' pun (reads as romance); Switch recuts and the second trailer are padding.
